source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014)

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: When teaching male condom use, why should the tip be pinched while unrolling it?
questions.rationale: Pressing the tip prevents air from collecting, which lowers the risk of breakage.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 7 Male condoms (PDF p. 156)
questions.quote: Pressing the tip prevents air accumulation.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: A client asks which lubricant is safe with latex condoms. The nurse recommends:
questions.rationale: Water-based lubricants are safe; oils and lotions damage latex.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 7 Condom counseling (PDF p. 159)
questions.quote: Advise users not to use cooking oil, baby oil, coconut oil, or skin lotion as a lubricant

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: After ejaculation, the man should withdraw while:
questions.rationale: Hold the rim at the base and withdraw before the erection is lost so the condom does not slip off.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 7 Male condoms (PDF p. 156)
questions.quote: hold the rim of the condom at the base of the penis so it will not slip off

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Which client should be advised to use condoms after vasectomy?
questions.rationale: Post-vasectomy clients use condoms until a semen check after 3 months confirms azoospermia.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 7 Who can use the male condom (PDF p. 157)
questions.quote: Postvasectomy clients who are waiting for sperm check or semen analysis after three months

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: A man says condoms will make him impotent. The nurse's best reply is:
questions.rationale: Condoms do not cause impotence, sterility or weakness; more lubrication may help sensation.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 7 Condom FAQs (PDF p. 161)
questions.quote: Condoms do not cause impotence.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: How long before sex may a female condom be inserted?
questions.rationale: The female condom may be inserted up to 8 hours before sex, before any genital contact.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 7 Female condoms (PDF p. 163)
questions.quote: Insert the condom within 8 hours before sex.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: How long must a diaphragm stay in place after intercourse?
questions.rationale: Leave the diaphragm at least 6 hours after sex but no longer than 24 hours.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 7 Diaphragm (PDF p. 168)
questions.quote: Keep the diaphragm in place for at least 6 hours after having sex but no longer than 24 hours.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: A woman who gave birth 3 weeks ago wants a diaphragm. The nurse advises:
options: Fit it at 6 weeks or later
questions.rationale: The diaphragm is fitted at least 6 weeks after a term birth, when the uterus and cervix return to normal size.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 7 Diaphragm counseling (PDF p. 170)
questions.quote: The diaphragm should be fitted at least six weeks after childbirth

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Which client is advised against using a diaphragm?
options: Woman at high risk of HIV
questions.rationale: Diaphragms and cervical caps are not advised for women with HIV or at high risk; offer condoms.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 7 Diaphragm (PDF p. 168)
questions.quote: Women with HIV infection or at high risk of HIV infection are not advised to use the diaphragm.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Which is the only calendar-based method recommended by the DOH?
questions.rationale: Of the calendar-based methods, the SDM is the only DOH-recommended one.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 8 FAB methods (PDF p. 179)
questions.quote: The SDM is the only DOH-recommended method.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Which woman is a suitable candidate for the Standard Days Method?
questions.rationale: SDM works for women whose cycles are 26 to 32 days long.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 8 Standard Days Method (PDF p. 185)
questions.quote: The SDM works well for women who usually have menstrual cycles that are 26 to 32 days long.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: An SDM user is on day 12 of her cycle (white bead). The couple should:
questions.rationale: Days 8 to 19 (white beads) are fertile; avoid sex or use a barrier.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 8 Using the SDM (PDF p. 186)
questions.quote: Days 8 to 19 of every cycle (when the ring is on the white beads) are considered fertile days

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: An SDM user had two cycles longer than 32 days in the past year. The nurse suggests:
questions.rationale: Two or more cycles outside 26–32 days in 12 months: suggest a symptoms-based method.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 8 SDM problems (PDF p. 187)
questions.quote: If the client has two or more cycles outside the 26–32 day range within any 12 months

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: A Two-Day Method user noticed secretions yesterday but none today. Today she is:
questions.rationale: Any secretions today or yesterday mean she may be fertile today; two dry days in a row are needed.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 8 Two-Day Method (PDF p. 190)
questions.quote: If a woman notices any secretions today or yesterday, she should consider herself fertile

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: In the Billings Ovulation Method, the 'peak day' is the:
questions.rationale: Peak day is the last day of clear, slippery, stretchy mucus; abstain for 3 more days.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 8 Billings Ovulation Method (PDF p. 193)
questions.quote: the last day that the client secretes clear, slippery, stretchy, and wet mucus

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Using the Billings method, when may unprotected sex resume after the peak day?
questions.rationale: She is fertile for 3 days after the peak; sex may resume on the 4th day until the next menses.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 8 Billings Ovulation Method (PDF p. 193)
questions.quote: Unprotected sex can be resumed on the fourth day after the woman's peak day

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: When should a woman take her basal body temperature?
questions.rationale: BBT is taken at the same time each morning after at least 3 hours of sleep, before getting out of bed.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 8 BBT method (PDF p. 195)
questions.quote: The client takes her body temperature at the same time each morning before she gets out of bed

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: The rise in basal body temperature after ovulation is caused by:
questions.rationale: Progesterone after ovulation raises BBT by 0.2–0.5 °C until the next menses.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 8 BBT method (PDF p. 194)
questions.quote: stays high until the next menstruation because of a rise in progesterone level

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: A BBT user's temperature has stayed raised for 3 full days. This means:
questions.rationale: A raised BBT for 3 full days shows ovulation occurred; unprotected sex may resume on day 4.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 8 BBT method (PDF p. 195)
questions.quote: stayed high for three full days indicates that ovulation has occurred and that the fertile period has passed

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Which mother meets all three criteria for LAM?
questions.rationale: LAM requires no return of menses, full or nearly full breastfeeding, and a baby under 6 months.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 9 LAM (PDF p. 197)
questions.quote: the baby is less than six months old

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: For LAM to stay effective, night feedings should be no more than how many hours apart?
questions.rationale: Day feeds no more than 4 hours apart; night feeds no more than 6 hours apart.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 9 LAM use (PDF p. 198)
questions.quote: night-time feedings should not be more than six hours apart

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: A LAM user's baby turns 6 months old. What does the nurse advise?
questions.rationale: When any LAM criterion is no longer met, she must switch to another method; breastfeeding continues.
questions.source: DOH Philippine Clinical Standards Manual on Family Planning (2014), Ch. 9 Switching from LAM (PDF p. 200)
questions.quote: the client must switch to another method as soon as any of the three LAM criteria no longer applies
